subject: general
question: A constant force acts on an object of mass 10 kg for a duration of 2 seconds. It increases the object's velocity from 5 metres/second to 10 metres /second. Find the magnitude of the applied force. Now, if the force is applied for a duration of 5 seconds, what would be the final velocity of the object?

options.text: Applied Force = 25 N, Final Velocity = 17.5 metres/second
Applied Force = 20 N, Final Velocity = 7.5 metres/second
Applied Force = 25 N, Final Velocity = 7.5 metres/second
Applied Force = 20 N, Final Velocity = 17.5 metres/second

solution:
The correct answer is __Applied Force = 25 N, Final Velocity = 17.5 metres/second__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• According to Newton’s Second Law, Force (F) = mass (m) × acceleration (a).

**Given:**

 
• Mass, m = 10 kg,
 
• Initial velocity, u = 5 m/s,
 
• Final velocity, v = 10 m/s,
 
• Time, t = 2 s.
 
• So, Acceleration a = (v-u)/t
 
• a = (10 − 5)/2 = 2.5 m/s².
 
• Applied Force F = 10 kg × 2.5 m/s² = 25 N.

Now, if the same force is applied for 5 seconds, acceleration remains 2.5 m/s², and initial velocity is 5 m/s.

 
• Final velocity v = u + at = 5 + (2.5 × 5) = 17.5 m/s.
